objectives.text: Explain how young animals are similar to their parents
Explain how young animals grow and change into adults

keyIdeas.statement: Young animals are similar to their parents because they are the same kind of animal.
keyIdeas.explanation: A kitten and its cat parent both have fur, whiskers, four legs and a tail. A chick and its hen parent both have feathers, wings and a beak.
keyIdeas.example: A puppy is similar to its dog parent because both have fur, four legs, ears and a tail.

keyIdeas.statement: Young animals may look smaller or different, but they still have features like their parents.
keyIdeas.explanation: A young animal does not need to look exactly like its parent. It has some of the same body parts and features.
keyIdeas.example: A duckling is smaller than a duck, but both have feathers, wings, a beak and webbed feet.

misconceptions.belief: A young animal must look exactly the same as its parent.
misconceptions.correction: Young animals can be smaller or have different colours, but they have some of the same features as their parents.

vocabulary.definition: A part or quality of an animal that can be seen.

questions.stem: Which young animal is similar to a cat parent?
questions.reasoning: A kitten and a cat have fur, four legs, ears and a tail.

questions.stem: Give two features that a puppy and its dog parent may both have.
questions.reasoning: Both animals are dogs, so they can share features such as fur and four legs.

questions.stem: True or false: A duckling cannot be similar to a duck because it is smaller.
questions.reasoning: A duckling can be smaller but still share features such as feathers, wings and a beak.

questions.stem: A chick and a kitten are both small. Which is the best reason they are not the same kind of animal?
questions.answer: They have different features and parents
questions.reasoning: Animals of the same kind share features with their parents; chicks and kittens do not share the same features or parents.

keyIdeas.statement: Young animals are similar to their parents because they are the same kind of animal.
keyIdeas.explanation: A young animal has many of the same body features as its parent, such as fur, feathers, wings or a beak.
keyIdeas.example: A kitten has fur, four legs and a tail, like its cat parent.

keyIdeas.statement: Young animals can look smaller than their parents but still share the same features.
keyIdeas.explanation: A puppy may be smaller than an adult dog, but both have fur, four legs, a tail and a nose.
keyIdeas.example: A chick has feathers, wings and a beak, like its chicken parent.

misconceptions.belief: A young animal is a different kind of animal from its parent.
misconceptions.correction: A young animal is the same kind of animal as its parent, even if it looks smaller or has softer features.

vocabulary.definition: A part or detail of an animal, such as fur, wings or a beak.

questions.stem: What is one feature that a kitten and its cat parent can both have?
questions.reasoning: Both animals can have fur because they are the same kind of animal.

questions.stem: Why is a puppy similar to its dog parent?
questions.answer: They have some of the same features
questions.reasoning: A puppy and a dog are the same kind of animal, so they share body features.

questions.stem: True or false: A chick is a different kind of animal from a chicken because it is young.
questions.reasoning: A chick is a young chicken, so it is the same kind of animal as its parent.

questions.stem: A baby penguin and an adult penguin look different in size. Give one reason they are still the same kind of animal.
questions.answer: They share features such as a beak, wings or feathers
questions.reasoning: Sharing body features shows that they are the same kind of animal.
